channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakh Language Integrated into WIPO's AI Subtitling System for First Time
item.description: The Kazakh language has been included in the World Intellectual Property Organization's (WIPO) experimental AI-based subtitling system. It is now among 20 available languages, enabling real-time translation of discussions for Kazakh speakers at international forums. This marks a significant step in expanding the language's digital presence.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Signals Further Migration Policy Reforms by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced further changes to the migration system by 2027, following two previous reforms. This comes amid reported corruption issues within the migration agency. The president emphasized creating conditions that value human dignity and ensuring migrants' rights abroad.

item.title: Russia Claims Air Defenses Destroyed 155 Ukrainian Drones Overnight
item.description: Russia's Ministry of Defence reported that its air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 155 Ukrainian drones across various regions overnight. The attacks reportedly caused minor damage and one injury in the Smolensk and Novgorod regions. This incident is part of ongoing tensions and failed peace efforts between Russia and Ukraine.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Arrives in Moscow for Security Council Meeting
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Moscow to participate in a session of the Collective Security Council of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). He was met by Russian government officials at the airport. The purpose of his visit is to attend the CSTO meeting.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Investigate Yandex's Data Security Practices
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development will conduct an unscheduled inspection of Yandex's legal entities, including Yandex Kazakhstan, Yandex Go, and Yandex Food Kazakhstan, by the end of November. The probe aims to determine where Kazakhstani citizens' personal data is stored and how it is protected. Violations could lead to administrative liability.

item.title: UN Women: Over One-Third of Global Women Live in Climate-Vulnerable Areas
item.description: UN Women reports that over 1.5 billion women and girls worldwide reside in areas susceptible to climate change risks. The climate crisis, coupled with insecure employment and gender inequality, poses serious threats. While most countries acknowledge these risks, few have implemented comprehensive measures to address them.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Pilot Project for Online IIN Registration for Foreigners
item.description: Kazakhstan is piloting a project allowing foreigners and stateless persons to obtain and modify their Individual Identification Numbers (IIN) online via the QazETA mobile app. The service, available through the MAQ digital platform, requires biometric identification and checks entry data. The processing time is one working day.

item.title: Putin Urges CSTO to Enhance Military Cooperation Amid International Tensions
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin called for the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) to increase its potential and strengthen military interaction due to ongoing international tensions. He emphasized the need for active cooperation in defense, counter-terrorism, cybercrime, drug trafficking, and illegal migration. A CSTO summit is scheduled for November 11 in Moscow.

item.title: Turkmenistan's TAPI Gas Pipeline Nears Afghan City, Commissioning by End of 2026
item.description: Turkmenistan announced the TAPI gas pipeline has reached the outskirts of Herat, Afghanistan, and is expected to be commissioned by the end of 2026. Satellite images confirm the pipeline extends from Turkmenistan's border to a construction zone west of Herat. The project, envisioned in the 1990s, aims to connect Turkmenistan's gas fields to Afghanistan, Pakistan, and India.

item.title: Tashkent Region Strengthens Partnership with Japan Through Working Visit
item.description: A delegation from the Tashkent region, led by khokim Zoyir Mirzaev, is on a working visit to Japan to enhance interregional cooperation and attract Japanese investment. Discussions focused on joint projects in automotive, electrical, industrial equipment, and construction materials, as well as agricultural development and innovation exchange. Educational ties with Japanese universities were also explored.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Discuss Digital Security for Youth at Media Forum
item.description: A seminar on 'Information Security in Cyberspace and Child Protection' was held during the third Uzbek-Russian Media Forum. Participants discussed the growing influence of the digital environment on youth, risks of destructive online communities, and the role of the state, family, and media in ensuring a safe digital space. Media literacy and international cooperation were also highlighted.

item.title: Uzbekistan Seeks U.S. Investment for Infrastructure Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan is seeking American financing and technology for its electricity networks, data centers, and transport infrastructure. A delegation led by the Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade met with U.S. business leaders in Washington to discuss mutually beneficial partnerships. Upgrades to electricity transmission and distribution are estimated to cost at least $5 billion.

item.title: Trump Faces Difficult Choices on Iran War: Internal Disagreement Over Resource Allocation
item.description: President Trump faces four difficult choices regarding a potential war with Iran, with internal disagreements arising over resource allocation. Vice President Mike Pence and Secretary of War Mark Esper are reportedly in conflict over the strategy. Each proposed military and diplomatic scenario carries significant financial and political risks for the US.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Officially Seeks Second Term
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's incumbent President Sadyr Japarov has officially declared his intention to run for a second term. He submitted his application to the Central Election Commission on November 10th, becoming the sixth candidate. Presidential elections are scheduled for January 27, 2027, with candidate nominations closing on November 13th.

item.title: Shymkent Hosts Discussion on Implementing President's Address on Welfare and Healthcare
item.description: In Shymkent, officials including MP Bakhadyr Narimbetov and Health Ministry representative Bauyrzhan Zhusupov met with residents to discuss the President's Address on Kazakhstan's urgent tasks. Emphasis was placed on economic development, citizen welfare, and improving living standards, with calls for active citizen participation in reforms.

item.title: US Democrats Plan $15 Billion Aid Package for Ukraine
item.description: US Democrats, holding a congressional advantage, are discussing a new military aid package for Ukraine valued at approximately $15 billion. Priorities include energy sector support before winter, supplying air defense interceptor missiles, intelligence assistance, and ensuring the Starlink satellite system's functionality.

item.title: Kazakh Language Integrated into UN AI Translation System
item.description: Kazakh has been included in the experimental artificial intelligence-based automatic translation system of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO). This integration allows Kazakh scientists and officials to follow international discussions in real-time. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan stated this is a result of efforts to promote the language internationally.

item.title: Orphan Wins Lawsuit Against Housing Bank, Restores 11 Years in Queue
item.description: A former boarding school student in Kostanay region has won a lawsuit against 'Otbasy Bank', restoring 11 years to his housing queue. He proved his right to have his registration date corrected from 2020 to 2009, when he became eligible as an orphan. The court approved a mediation agreement where the bank conceded to the demands.

item.title: Wife of Detained Ex-MP Accuses President of Interference in Case
item.description: The wife of detained former MP Maksat Kunakunov has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov, claiming her husband is illegally held and that a citizen who defrauded them is influencing the investigation using the president's name. She alleges the investigation is unfair and one-sided, seeking the president's help.

item.title: Georgia Deports 91 Foreign Nationals, Including Uzbek Citizens, Banning Re-entry
item.description: Georgia's Ministry of Internal Affairs has deported 91 foreign citizens, including individuals from Uzbekistan, and banned them from re-entering the country. This action is part of intensified measures against illegal migration, with stricter legislation simplifying deportation procedures. Citizens from Azerbaijan, Armenia, Egypt, India, Jordan, Iraq, China, Congo, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Sudan, Tajikistan, Thailand, Turkmenistan, Turkey, and Uganda were also expelled.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sought Since 2014 Returned from USA
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, wanted since 2014 for illegally leaving Uzbekistan, has been apprehended in the USA and returned to his home country. The individual, identified as Yu. N., born in 1978, is accused of violating border crossing procedures for officials requiring special agreements. He was handed over to the Jizzakh city prosecutor's office upon his return. Further details of the case were not disclosed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Constitutional Court Adopts Electronic Case Management System
item.description: A new Constitutional Law on the Constitutional Court of the Republic of Uzbekistan has come into force, introducing electronic case management. This reform aims to enhance constitutional justice, protect citizens' rights, and improve court operations. Key changes include updated procedures for appeals, case review, digital technology integration, open hearings, and enforcement of judicial acts. The law clarifies the procedural status of parties and witnesses.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Upholds Arrest of Environmentalist Laura Malikova for Organizing Protests
item.description: An appeals court in Astana has upheld the administrative arrest of Laura Malikova, head of the Association of Practicing Ecologists. She was detained for 10 days on November 3 for allegedly organizing illegal rallies. The court found her Instagram post calling for protests violated regulations on peaceful assembly.

item.title: Kazakhstan: 87 Million Tenge Fraud Discovered in Road Repair Project
item.description: Authorities in North Kazakhstan region have uncovered fraud amounting to 87 million tenge during a road repair project. The funds were allocated for the 'Timiryazevo – Dokuchaevo' highway. A former head of the contracting organization is suspected of embezzlement. The suspect has been detained pending investigation into large-scale fraud.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Currency Exchange Rates: Ruble Falls, Euro Exceeds 98 Som
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan set official exchange rates for November 11, 2026. The Russian ruble continued its decline, falling to 1.0570 som. The Euro, however, rose by 0.55% to exceed 98 som. The US dollar remained stable, while the Chinese yuan and Kazakh tenge strengthened.

item.title: Taliban Justice Ministry Arrests Township Representatives Again Amid Land Dispute
item.description: Sources report the Taliban's Ministry of Justice has again arrested representatives from Kabul's Omid Sabz Township. Four Hazara and Shia figures were summoned and detained, with their whereabouts currently unknown. This follows previous arrests and ongoing tensions over the ministry's claim that the township's land is state-owned.

item.title: Tajikistan President Urges Police to Treat Public with Respect
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon has again called on police officers nationwide to interact respectfully with citizens. A former investigator suggests that blaming only ordinary police officers is unfair. The call comes amid ongoing discussions about police conduct and public trust in the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan reduces power plant wear to 52% amid heating season preparations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy reports that wear on power plants has decreased to 52%, and electrical grids to 65.7%. The ministry stated that repair work funding increased by 27%, with significant progress made on power units, boilers, and turbines. Technological violations decreased by 6%.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Investigate Five Yandex Companies Over Data Protection
item.description: Kazakhstan will conduct unscheduled inspections of five companies affiliated with Yandex. The Ministry of Digital Development aims to verify their compliance with personal data storage and protection requirements. The investigation, expected to conclude by the end of November, will examine how citizen data is handled and secured within Kazakhstan.

item.title: Astana Opens Exhibition Connecting Past and Present Through Tulips
item.description: The National Museum in Astana has opened an exhibition titled 'Homeland of Tulips,' dedicated to the 35th anniversary of Kazakhstan's independence. The exhibition by artist Kazakbay Azhibekuly uses the tulip motif to symbolize national resilience and the pursuit of freedom, linking historical figures with modern Kazakhstan.

item.title: Pneumonia Cases Rise Among Afghan Children Amidst Poverty and Cold
item.description: Residents in Kabul report a surge in pneumonia cases among children as temperatures drop, with many families lacking funds for treatment. The lack of adequate facilities in public hospitals exacerbates the crisis, leading to preventable deaths. Air pollution from winter heating and traffic further complicates the health situation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Remove All IQAir Air Quality Monitoring Sensors
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to dismantle all IQAir air quality sensors, having already removed six of the twelve installed devices. The Ministry of Natural Resources cites significant discrepancies between IQAir data and official meteorological service readings, deeming the former unreliable. Concerns remain about actual air pollution levels and respiratory illnesses.

item.title: U.S. Secretary Rubio Expands Engagement in Central Asia with Samarkand Visit
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Samarkand, Uzbekistan, to deepen diplomatic and commercial ties, accompanied by over 200 American business representatives. Discussions focused on investment, critical minerals, infrastructure, and regional security, following a significant C5+1 summit in Washington. This signals an increasing economic focus in U.S. regional policy.

item.title: Four Books on Exile, Violence, and Rights Shortlisted for Moore Prize
item.description: Four books exploring themes of wrongful conviction, gun violence, life in exile, and a militant attack in Mozambique have been shortlisted for the 2026 Moore Prize for Human Rights Writing. The winner will be announced on January 6, 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces SMS System for Reporting Fake Vaccination Records
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched an SMS service allowing citizens to verify vaccination records and report discrepancies. After vaccination, individuals will receive an SMS from 1414; replying with '811' confirms the record, while '812' indicates a false entry. This aims to identify and correct inaccuracies in the vaccination database.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Russia's Membership in Turkic States Organization
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed admitting Russia into the Organization of Turkic States. Turkey views this proposal with skepticism, while Azerbaijan believes Russia's closer ties could impact Turkic unity. The feasibility of Kazakhstan's proposal remains uncertain.

item.title: Uzbekistan Urged to Investigate Red Book Bird Hunting Videos
item.description: Videos circulating on social media showing hunting of birds listed in Uzbekistan's Red Book have prompted calls for an investigation. Users highlighted potential violations of environmental laws. While pheasant hunting is shown, there is no definitive proof of illegal activity yet. Authorities are urged to assess the situation.

item.title: US Immigration Crackdown Affects Uzbek Nationals Amid Fraud Allegations
item.description: Reports detail criminal cases involving Uzbek nationals in the US, including multi-million dollar health insurance fraud and cargo theft. These cases emerge as the Trump administration intensifies immigration enforcement. The circumstances surrounding a fatal road accident involving Uzbeks are also under scrutiny.

item.title: Taliban Confirm Arrest of Former Republic Military Official
item.description: The Taliban government has confirmed the arrest of Allahdad Fedaee, a former military official of the ousted republic. Fedaee's alleged confession video, implicating him in planning attacks against the Taliban, recently surfaced online. The United Front for Afghanistan acknowledged Fedaee as a trusted commander but stated he had not yet participated in military operations.

item.title: Tajik President Urges Police Politeness; Tajik Prisoners Fear Ukraine Deployment
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon has called on police to be more courteous to citizens. Meanwhile, Tajik prisoners in Russia reportedly fear being sent to fight in Ukraine. The European Union sees significant potential for cooperation with Tajikistan. A group of Tajik civil activists held a rally in Germany.
